title: Sentence Synthesis
description: Master sentence synthesis for Grade 10 (ICSE): combining sentences using participles, infinitives, relative pronouns, apposition, abstract nouns and conjunctions — bilingual notes and tests.

topics.title: Synthesis by Participle, Infinitive & Conjunction
topics.concept:
Participle: turn one action into an -ing/-ed phrase.

  • He finished his food. He left. → Having finished his food, he left.
  • The work was done. He rested. → The work done, he rested.

Infinitive: use 'to + verb', often to show purpose or with too/enough.

  • He was very tired. He could not walk. → He was too tired to walk.
  • She studied hard. She wanted to pass. → She studied hard to pass.

Conjunction: join with a coordinating or subordinating conjunction.

  • He is poor. He is honest. → He is poor but honest.
  • It rained. We stayed in. → As it rained, we stayed in.

examples.problem: Synthesise (participle): She heard the news. She fainted.
Synthesise (infinitive): He was rich enough. He could buy the car.
examples.solution: He was rich enough to buy the car.

recap: Participle: turn one action into an -ing/-ed phrase
Infinitive: 'to + verb' for purpose or with too/enough
Conjunction: join with and/but or because/as/though

topics.title: Synthesis by Relative Pronoun, Apposition & Abstract Noun
topics.concept:
Relative pronoun: turn one sentence into a who/which/that clause.

  • This is the boy. He won the prize. → This is the boy who won the prize.

Apposition (a noun phrase placed beside another, set off by commas):

  • He is the captain. He is the best player. → He, the captain, is the best player.

Abstract noun: turn an adjective/quality into a noun that becomes the subject or cause.

  • She was very kind. She helped everyone. → Her kindness made her help everyone.
  • He is honest. Everyone trusts him. → His honesty wins everyone's trust.

Noun/adjective phrase: reduce a clause to a phrase — The man, being poor, could not pay.

examples.problem: Synthesise (relative): I met a girl. She speaks five languages.
examples.solution: I met a girl who speaks five languages.

examples.problem: Synthesise (abstract noun): He was brave. It saved the village.

recap: Relative pronoun: who/which/that turns a sentence into a clause
Apposition: a noun phrase beside another, in commas
Abstract noun: a quality becomes a noun (kindness, honesty, bravery)

intro.en: Synthesis is the art of combining several short sentences into one well-made sentence — the opposite of analysis. ICSE papers test it directly. There are several methods (participle, infinitive, relative pronoun, apposition, abstract noun, conjunction), and the skill is choosing the one that joins the ideas most smoothly.
intro.hi: संश्लेषण (synthesis) कई छोटे वाक्यों को एक सुगठित वाक्य में जोड़ने की कला है — विश्लेषण का उल्टा। ICSE पेपर इसे सीधे जाँचते हैं। इसके कई तरीके हैं (participle, infinitive, relative pronoun, apposition, abstract noun, conjunction), और कौशल है वह तरीका चुनना जो विचारों को सबसे सहजता से जोड़े।

real_life.situation:
Three choppy facts become one smooth sentence:

Choppy: Ravi is a boy. He is brave. He saved a child.

Synthesised: Ravi, a brave boy, saved a child.
real_life.why: By turning 'He is brave' into the apposition 'a brave boy', three sentences become one elegant statement. Synthesis makes writing concise and mature — exactly what board examiners reward.

common_mistakes.wrong: Having finished her work and she left.
common_mistakes.right: Having finished her work, she left.
common_mistakes.note: Don't add 'and' after a participle phrase.

common_mistakes.wrong: He is too weak that he cannot walk.
This is the boy which won.
He, the captain is the best player.
common_mistakes.right: He, the captain, is the best player.
common_mistakes.note: An appositive needs commas on both sides.

reading.passage: Riya, a hardworking student, won the science prize. Having spent months on her project, she presented it confidently. The judges, who were strict, were impressed by her clarity. Her dedication earned everyone's respect. She was too modest to boast, and her humility made her even more admired.

questions.q: Identify the appositive phrase in the first sentence.
questions.answer: 'a hardworking student' — placed beside 'Riya', set off by commas.

questions.q: Find a participle phrase and explain its function.
questions.answer: 'Having spent months on her project' — it combines an earlier action with the main clause.

questions.q: Which abstract nouns combine ideas in the passage?
questions.answer: 'dedication' and 'humility' — qualities turned into nouns that drive the sentences.

writing.prompt: Take three short sentences of your own and combine them into one sentence using any synthesis method; then do it again using a different method.
writing.example: Sam is a boy. He is brave. He saved a dog. → Sam, a brave boy, saved a dog. / Being brave, Sam saved a dog.
